Seth Bodnar

Independent candidate for United States Senator, Montana · Open seat

Former president of the University of Montana; retired U.S. Army lieutenant colonel (Green Beret)

Seth Bodnar is a former U.S. Army Special Forces officer and former General Electric executive who served as president of the University of Montana from 2018 until January 2026. He resigned from the university and filed as an independent candidate for U.S. Senate on March 4, 2026, the last day of candidate filing, and needed about 13,000 voter signatures by May 26 to qualify for the general election ballot. He is on the November 3, 2026 ballot with Republican Kurt Alme, Democrat Alani Bankhead and Libertarian Kyle Austin.

Where Bodnar stands

War powers
Says declaring war is Congress's constitutional responsibility and argues that partisanship has led members of Congress to cede too much power to the executive branch.
Rural health care
Supports telehealth expansion and workforce incentives for rural health care. Opposes cuts to critical access hospitals and says he will defend Montana's Medicaid expansion.
Healthcare
Says the recent party-line budget bill will remove more than 30,000 Montanans from health coverage and cost rural hospitals more than $5 billion. Opposes cuts that would remove coverage.
Cost of living and housing
Supports building more homes by cutting red tape, using tax incentives and fixing supply chains. Supports rules to stop private equity firms from buying large numbers of single-family homes.
Trade and tariffs
Says tariffs should be strategic tools to open markets and protect key industries. Opposes the trade dispute with Canada and pledges to reassert Congress's authority over tariffs.
Immigration
Supports strong borders, enforcement of immigration law and comprehensive immigration reform. Says enforcement must respect due process and opposes use of what he calls an unaccountable, masked force.
Data centers
Supports strict federal guardrails so data centers cannot be built in Montana communities without community involvement, and to protect water supplies and electricity rates.
Abortion
Describes himself as a strong supporter of reproductive freedom. Says a woman's health decisions should be between her, her doctor, her family and her faith.
Public lands
Says protecting public lands is a top priority and calls them common ground where everyone can hunt, fish and recreate.
Guns
Says government has "no business" in Montanans' gun cabinets.

Background

  • President, University of Montana (2018–2026)
  • U.S. Army, 2003–2022 (101st Airborne Division, 1st Special Forces Group, Montana Army National Guard); retired as lieutenant colonel
  • Executive, General Electric
  • B.S., U.S. Military Academy at West Point; Rhodes Scholar, Hertford College, Oxford (graduate degrees)
